# Key conclusions

1. **Sensory responses are widespread but spatially organised.** Of 179,064 good and multi-unit neurons (122 sessions,
   92 mice), 15.3 % respond to the whisker stimulus and 15.2 % to the auditory stimulus in the active task (5-35 ms after
   onset); 27.8 % prefer one modality. Whisker-excited neurons concentrate in barrel cortex, SSs, the whisker motor
   cortices, dorsolateral striatum and the superior colliculus; auditory responses dominate in auditory cortex, the
   tail of the striatum and the midbrain (Section 3).
2. **Each modality reaches its own sensory system first.** Median half-time to peak of responsive neurons: whisker
   11.6 ms in whisker somatosensory cortex vs 18.0 ms for auditory responses there; auditory 8.5 ms in the midbrain vs
   16.9 ms for whisker responses there (Section 3.4).
3. **Whisker and auditory cortex project to partly overlapping targets.** In the Allen anterograde tracing data the
   70 % projection zones of whisker cortex (SSp-bfd + SSs, 29.4 mm³) and auditory cortex (AUDp + AUDd/v, 14.5 mm³)
   overlap in 3.9 mm³: mainly the caudal / tail striatum, posterior parietal cortex (VISa, VISrl, VISal), SCm, MRN
   and TEa (Section 4).
4. **Bimodal neurons are enriched where these projections converge.** 24.2 % of the sensory-responsive neurons respond to
   both modalities; inside the overlap zone 29.5 % do vs 23.8 % of all responsive neurons (+5.7 percentage points,
   95 % CI +1.1 to +10.3; hierarchical bootstrap p = 0.008; 90 % zones: +6.3 points, p < 0.001). This is a
   co-location, not evidence of causation (Section 5).
5. **Within areas, whisker- and auditory-preferring neurons are spatially offset.** In 10 of 13 target slabs the two
   populations differ in location by 70-710 µm (within-session permutation, Holm p < 0.05), e.g. auditory-preferring
   neurons lie deeper in SSp-bfd and SCm and more superficial in auditory cortex (Section 6).
6. **Stimulus modality can be decoded within 8-18 ms of stimulus onset, earliest in the midbrain.** With 200-neuron
   pseudo-populations the first significant 20-ms bin ends at 8 ms in the midbrain / SCm, 10 ms in whisker
   somatosensory cortex and thalamus, 12 ms in auditory cortex and the striatum and 14-18 ms in motor-frontal areas
   (ALM last). Earlier onset goes with higher early accuracy (Spearman ρ = -0.9), and at matched early accuracy the
   midbrain needs about 3 times fewer neurons than whisker cortex (Section 7).

**Status.** Pending: the ROC of three sessions with corrected context labels (maps and co-location will be refreshed),
the decoding sweep over all 18 area groups and the 40 best-sampled areas (this report shows the first 6 groups and 8
areas), and decoding of passive trials. Pseudo-population iterations (100 x 10 shuffles) are pilot values.

# Data

## Sessions, neurons and trials

- **Recordings.** Neuropixels recordings sorted with Kilosort 4 (NWB files, `NWB_ks4`); 122 whisker-training sessions
  (learning day and expert days, R+ and R- cohorts; 90 learning-day and 32 expert sessions; 68 R+ and 54 R- sessions;
  92 mice). Inclusion and cohort labels follow the dataset record (`skills/ssl-valid-data`).
- **Neurons.** Good and multi-unit clusters (`quality_label` from the v2 unit table, with the drift test); 179,064
  neurons. Positions: CCF coordinates of the probe-track reconstruction (`ccf_atlas_ap/ml/dv`, µm), folded onto one
  hemisphere. Areas: the custom area groups and areas of `allen_utils` (18 groups, 46 areas); a structure counts as
  recorded with at least 10 neurons (111 structures).
- **Trials.** Active trials: context active, `perf` ≠ 6, auditory warm-up block removed (keeping the trial before the
  first whisker trial), end-of-session disengagement trimmed (rule A1). Passive trials: trials in a fixed ~3 s ITI
  sequence or labelled passive (pre- and post-task blocks). Unlabelled trials in a session with context labels are
  active (one session, MH062 day +4).
- **Whisker artefact.** Spikes in -10 to +5 ms around every whisker-stimulus onset are replaced by a Poisson spike train
  at the neuron's pre-onset rate (-200 to -10 ms); all analyses use these corrected spike trains.

## Pooling

All analyses here pool both cohorts and both learning stages: the goal is to describe sensory responses, not their
change with learning. Cohort / stage splits are listed as next steps.

# Single-neuron sensory responses

## Responsiveness and modality preference (rate-based ROC)

For a neuron, a condition A (baseline) and B (response), the spike counts in the response window (5-35 ms after onset)
and the baseline window (-1 s to -15 ms before the trial) of each trial give the area under the ROC curve; the
selectivity is

$$ \mathrm{sel} = 2\,\mathrm{AUC}(A, B) - 1 \in [-1, 1], $$

positive when B is higher. Significance: 1000 label permutations, one-sided on the side of the observed selectivity,
p < 0.05. Quantities used:

| Quantity | A vs B | positive means |
|---|---|---|
| whisker responsiveness (`whisker_active`) | baseline vs whisker trials (active) | excited by whisker |
| auditory responsiveness (`auditory_active`) | baseline vs auditory trials (active) | excited by sound |
| modality preference (`wh_vs_aud_active`) | whisker vs auditory trials (active) | auditory-preferring |

Fractions significant: whisker 15.3 % (12.1 % excited, 3.2 % inhibited), auditory 15.2 % (13.6 % / 1.5 %),
modality 27.8 % (17.6 % auditory-preferring, 10.2 % whisker-preferring).

## Bimodal neurons

A neuron is responsive to modality $m$ if any of its stimulus-vs-baseline tests in the $k_m$ epochs available in its
session (active, passive pre, passive post; $k_m \in \{1,2,3\}$) is significant after Bonferroni correction:

$$ R_m = \exists\, e:\; p_{m,e} < 0.05 / k_m . $$

Bimodal: $R_\text{whisker} \wedge R_\text{auditory}$ (excited or inhibited). Of the 44,913 sensory-responsive neurons,
15,124 respond to whiskers only, 18,907 to sound only and 10,882 to both: bimodal fraction
$B = n_\text{both} / n_\text{responsive} = 24.2\,\%$.

## Response latency

For each responsive neuron and modality: PSTH in 1-ms bins (-100 to +200 ms, all trials of that modality), minus its
mean over -100 to -10 ms, smoothed (Gaussian, σ = 2 ms) and signed by the ROC selectivity $s$:
$r(t) = s\,[\mathrm{PSTH}(t) - \overline{\mathrm{PSTH}}_{[-100,-10]}]$. With $t_\text{peak} = \arg\max_{5 \le t \le 100} r(t)$,
the latency is the half-time to peak, the last upward crossing of $r(t) = r(t_\text{peak})/2$ before the peak (searched
after +5 ms for whisker trials, the end of the artefact window). Medians: whisker 17.4 ms (IQR 11.8-24.4, 24,200
neurons), auditory 15.2 ms (9.2-22.9, 26,639 neurons).

## Latency by area group

| Area group | whisker (ms) | auditory (ms) |
|---|---|---|
| Somatosensory-whisker | **11.6** | 18.0 |
| Posterior parietal | **12.6** | 16.7 |
| Auditory | 15.1 | 15.4 |
| Midbrain | 16.9 | **8.5** |
| Thalamus | 17.8 | 15.8 |
| Motor | 20.8 | 15.8 |
| Striatum | 21.1 | 16.5 |
| Frontal | 25.2 | 19.5 |

# Spatial organisation of sensory responses

## Maps: slabs, density and flatmaps

- **Slabs.** 500-µm-thick coronal slabs tiling the recorded AP range (16), sagittal slabs tiling the ML range (10),
  and 13 coronal slabs centred on projection zones / areas (SSp-bfd, SSs, wM1, wM2, ORB, anterior / caudal / tail of
  the striatum, SCm, AUDp, TEa, PO, MG). All neurons within ±250 µm are projected on the slab's central section.
- **Density (normalised by sampling).** Each quantity $q_i$ of neuron $i$ at position $x_i$ is summed on the 50-µm CCF grid
  and divided by the number of neurons with a value, both smoothed with the same 3-D Gaussian $G_\sigma$
  (σ = 150 µm):
  $$ \rho_q(x) = \frac{\left(G_\sigma * \sum_i q_i\, \delta_{x_i}\right)(x)}{\left(G_\sigma * \sum_i \delta_{x_i}\right)(x)}, $$
  averaged over the slab and shown where at least 3 neurons fall within the kernel. For the bimodal map, $q_i$ = 1 for
  bimodal and 0 for one-modality neurons, so $\rho$ is the local bimodal fraction.
- **Isocortex flatmap.** Allen CCFv3 butterfly flatmap (cortical streamlines from the Laplace solution between pia and
  white matter; 2-D coordinates from geodesic distances on the cortical surface to two pairs of anchor points; Wang
  et al. 2020, Harris et al. 2019), via Allen's `ccf_streamlines`. Each isocortex neuron (98,166) is placed at the flat
  position of its closest streamline (left hemisphere shown, anterior up). The embedding does not preserve area;
  numbers are computed in 3-D.

# Projection anatomy: where whisker and auditory cortex project

## Data and definitions

Allen Mouse Brain Connectivity Atlas, anterograde AAV tracing with the primary injection in the source area, wild-type
or Emx1-IRES-Cre mice (all cortical excitatory neurons): SSp-bfd 8 experiments, SSs 3, AUDp 6, AUDd + AUDv 3.
Projection density $d_e(v)$: fraction of voxel $v$ (50 µm) occupied by labelled axons in experiment $e$; injections
mirrored to one hemisphere. Candidate voxels $C$: ipsilateral brain, without fibre tracts, ventricles and the source
area itself. Per source:

$$ \bar D(v) = \frac{1}{E}\sum_{e=1}^{E} \frac{d_e(v)}{\sum_{v' \in C} d_e(v')}, \qquad \tilde D = G_{50\,\mu m} * \bar D . $$

**70 % zone.** $Z = \{v \in C : \tilde D(v) \ge \tau\}$ with $\tau$ such that $\sum_{v \in Z} \tilde D(v) = 0.7 \sum_{v \in C}
\tilde D(v)$: the highest-density voxels holding 70 % of the projection. Merged zones: whisker = mean of the SSp-bfd
and SSs densities, auditory = mean of AUDp and AUDd/v, each thresholded the same way; overlap = $Z_\text{whisker} \cap
Z_\text{auditory}$. The same analyses were repeated with 90 % zones.

## Results

Whisker-cortex zone 29.4 mm³, auditory-cortex zone 14.5 mm³, overlap 3.9 mm³ (almost all from SSp-bfd ∩ auditory
cortex). Largest pieces of the overlap: CP 0.87 mm³ (caudal and tail striatum), VISa 0.44 mm³ (61 % of VISa), VISrl
0.28, VISal 0.28 (74 % of VISal), SCm 0.21, MRN 0.17, TEa 0.16, SSp-tr 0.16. Composition of each zone: cortex 47-60 %,
striatum 8-20 %, thalamus 9-13 %, midbrain 6-30 % (auditory zones richest in midbrain: inferior and superior colliculus).

![**Projection zones of whisker and auditory cortex**, coronal 500-µm slabs. Rows: SSp-bfd, SSs, AUDp, AUDd + AUDv
(density, white = none; black line: 70 % contour; grey: injected area, excluded) and the overlap of the merged zones.
Labels: structures holding most of the zone in the slab; right: largest recorded structures as % of the zone volume.](fig/projection_zones_coronal.png){width=100%}

![Same, sagittal 500-µm slabs.](fig/projection_zones_sagittal.png){width=100%}

**What the anatomy can and cannot say.** The zones come from other mice and pool intratelencephalic, pyramidal-tract and
corticothalamic axons (including axons of passage); overlap marks where inputs from the two cortices *can* converge.

# Bimodal neurons and projection convergence (co-location)

## Definitions and test

Sensory-responsive neurons with their CCF position; $P_\text{in}$ = bimodal fraction among responsive neurons inside the
overlap, $P_\text{ref}$ = among all responsive neurons, $\Delta = P_\text{in} - P_\text{ref}$. Main test: hierarchical
bootstrap over sessions then neurons ($B$ = 2000): sessions resampled with replacement, binomial resampling of each
session's counts inside and outside, $\Delta^*_b$ recomputed;

$$ p = \frac{1 + \#\{b: \Delta^*_b \le 0\}}{1 + B} \quad\text{(one-sided)}, $$

95 % CI from the percentiles of $\Delta^*$. Fisher's exact test (neurons treated as independent) is reported alongside.
Overlap sub-regions (the overlap cut by structure into connected 3-D pieces ≥ 0.04 mm³, with ≥ 10 recorded neurons)
are described, not tested.

## Results

Inside the overlap 29.5 % of 3,292 responsive neurons (97 sessions, 75 mice) are bimodal vs 23.8 % of all 41,621:
$\Delta$ = +5.7 points (95 % CI +1.1 to +10.3), bootstrap p = 0.008 (Fisher p < 0.001). With 90 % zones:
29.3 % vs 23.0 %, +6.3 points (+2.6 to +9.6), p < 0.001.

# When does stimulus information arrive? Pseudo-population decoding

## Method

- **Data.** Whisker vs auditory active trials (all trials, lick or not), all sessions pooled, good + mua neurons,
  artefact-corrected spikes; a session is eligible for an area with ≥ 5 neurons there and ≥ 3 trials per class.
- **Pseudo-population (one iteration).** 20 sessions drawn with replacement; $N/20$ neurons of the area drawn within each
  session (with replacement); pseudo-trials built per class by concatenating one trial of that class per session
  (balanced reuse of each session's trials). $N$ = 20, 50, 100, 200, 300, 500.
- **Decoder.** For each time bin, L2-regularised logistic regression on z-scored rates; 3-fold cross-validation built on
  each session's real trials (100 training and 100 test pseudo-trials per class), regularisation chosen by an inner
  2-fold split. Balanced accuracy $\mathrm{BA} = \tfrac12(\mathrm{TPR} + \mathrm{TNR})$.
- **Null and corrected accuracy.** The same draw is re-decoded $K$ = 10 times with labels shuffled within sessions (same
  regularisation): $d(t) = \mathrm{BA}_\text{real}(t) - \frac{1}{K}\sum_k \mathrm{BA}_{\text{shuffle},k}(t)$ (0 = chance,
  0.5 = perfect). 100 iterations.
- **Time bins.** Causal bins labelled at their end: 50-ms bins in 5-ms steps (-200 to +600 ms) and 20-ms bins in 2-ms steps
  (-20 to +100 ms) for the first 50 ms.
- **Above chance.** Bin $t$ is above chance when the 5th percentile of $d(t)$ over iterations is > 0.
- **Onset.** $t_\text{on} = \min\{t > 0 : t \text{ above chance and} \ge 80\,\% \text{ of the bins in } [t, t+25\,\text{ms}]
  \text{ above chance}\}$ (20-ms bins); 95 % range from 1000 resamples of the iterations.
- **Early accuracy.** Mean $d$ over the 20-ms bins ending 5-50 ms after onset. **Matched neurons:** the $N$ an area
  needs to reach the early accuracy of a reference area at 100 neurons, interpolated linearly in $\log N$.

# Caveats and next steps

- **Co-location, not causation.** Projection zones come from other mice and include axons of passage; CCF positions of
  recorded neurons carry an uncertainty of about 100-200 µm.
- **Pooled cohorts and stages.** Split by cohort (R+ / R-) and stage (learning / expert) to check that pooling does not
  hide differences.
- **Lick confound in decoding.** Auditory trials are nearly always licked; after ~100 ms the decoder can use lick
  preparation. Passive-trial decoding (running) and licked-trials-only decoding address this; onsets in the first 20 ms
  are unaffected.
- **Artefact handling.** Whisker-trial spikes in -10 to +5 ms are replaced by baseline-rate Poisson spikes: onsets cannot
  fall before ~5 ms on whisker trials. A version with the window excised would test the earliest onsets.
- **Pilot sampling.** 100 iterations x 10 shuffles; increase before final figures.
- **Pending.** ROC of 3 context-corrected sessions; all 18 area groups and 40 best-sampled areas; passive-trial decoding.

| ROC response window | 5-35 ms; baseline -1 s to -15 ms; 1000 permutations; p < 0.05 |

| latency | half-time to peak, 1-ms PSTH, σ 2 ms, peak in 5-100 ms |
| slabs | 500 µm; density σ 150 µm (3-D), ≥ 3 neurons |
